newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says 4 foreign banks up for Luz del Sur sale.
newsitem.headline: Peru says 4 foreign banks up for Luz del Sur sale.

text.p: Four foreign investment banks are competing to handle the international placement of state-held shares in Peru's electricity distributor Luz del Sur, the government said Friday.
Peru will choose on September 10 between CS First Boston, Kleynwort Benson, JP Morgan and Merrill Lynch, the government announced in its newspaper El Peruano.
In July, JP Morgan and Merrill Lynch handled the international placement of a $1.25 billion sale of a 26.6 percent state-held stake in Telefonica del Peru.
The sale of the government's 30 percent stake in Luz del Sur will go ahead before the end of the year in three separate portions, according to the government.
As well as the international placement, the government has chosen local bank Banco Continental to coordinate the domestic sale that, in turn, is divided in two parts.

In the first of these - the sale of shares to individual Peruvian nationals under a "Citizens' Participation in Privatization" scheme - Banco Continental itself will direct a group of local banks that includes Banco de Credito, Interbanc and Banco Wiese.
In the second part of the local sale, Spain's Banco Santander has been selected to handle the placement with local institutions.

The Spanish bank's brokerage in Peru - Santander SAB - will direct a group of local brokerages to book build with institutions such as local pension funds, insurance companies and banks, privatization officials have said.

In June 1994, a consortium consisting of Chile's Chilquinta International Inc. and Canada's Ontario Hydro Inc. bought a 60 percent stake in Luz del Sur, a former state-run electricity company for $212.1 million.
Another 10 percent stake is owned by the company's workers.
